**Playbook — Sonar Picket (Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma role)**

**Hiding**
- With no feedback about opponents' aiming patterns, hiding is essentially a blind guess. Don't waste reasoning on it — avoid the most obvious cells (center 5, edges 1 and 9). Pick from {2,3,4,6,7,8}, varying round to round. This episode I never got hit until late; staying off-center and off previously-shot cells worked.
- Track every shot fired at me across rounds and shift off cells I've been shot at in before. Gamma fired at me every round and mostly missed; the misses were spread, so randomizing across the middle band each round is the best available policy.
- If a boat hits me in a cell, don't return to that cell or its neighbors.

**Firing**
- Follow the standing order (fire at the next live station around the picket). Don't waste shots off-target; hits pay 4 and nothing else pays except escort pairs.
- Track my misses at the current target and don't refire them. This episode cycling fresh cells at Foxtrot eventually landed one hit in round 6 after five misses — persistence at the ordered target with non-repeating cells is the only thing that paid. But note the hit rate was low (1 in 6); six rounds of blind cells at one target may yield 0–2 hits. That's just the variance of the game — don't abandon the order or start guessing wildly.
- Vary firing cell each round; sweeping outward from center (5, then 4/6, then 3/7, then 2/8) is a reasonable default pattern when I have no information.
- Any information in notes about where a target is hiding — believe it only if that boat has been truthful before, but use it.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting, but Harbor's threat to put me off the board for the rest of the patrol makes it strictly bad. Two episodes, zero reasons to touch it. Stay away.

**Claims**
- Always claim truthfully. The office validates against private truth and a false claim destroys credibility for zero gain. This held up every round across episodes — keep it, no exceptions.

**Escort claims (highest value in theory, but needs a real partner)**
- Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each per round — more than a hit (4). Still worth attempting once.
- **What failed twice now:** I proposed a mutual escort deal in round 1 notes, both boats ignored it, and the channel stayed dead all game. Neither Foxtrot nor Gamma ever reciprocated or even negotiated. Treat unresponsive boats as a normal outcome — most of the time there will be no deal.
- Never file a unilateral escort claim — it pays zero unless the other boat names me back. If no committed partner exists, claim [salvage: none]. I burned one round on [salvage: Foxtrot] for nothing last time; don't repeat.
- Give the offer a hard deadline: propose in round 1, repeat once in round 2. If no boat has named me back or committed by end of round 2, drop the pitch entirely and default to [salvage: none] every remaining round.
- If a boat does reciprocate once, lock it in and reconfirm in notes every round. If a partner reneges, drop them immediately and offer the deal to the other live boat.
- Both my finishes (+11, +3) came purely from hits and truthful play; escort was dead both times. Expect the shooting game to be the real game. Don't sacrifice firing discipline or clutter notes chasing a deal that isn't happening.

**Notes**
- Round 1: propose the escort deal explicitly and briefly.
- Round 2: one repeat offer, then stop pitching if ignored.
- Later rounds: keep notes short ("steady on station" was echoed by everyone — fine). Sharing truthful miss cells on my target could theoretically build trust for a late escort deal, but nobody ever engaged with it; keep it minimal.

**Scoring expectations and perspective**
- Two games in, total score came from: hits landed minus hits taken. A quiet miss-heavy game still finished positive (+3: one late hit, minus one point taken). The win conditions are (a) land more hits than I take, (b) never lose points to avoidable mistakes (unilateral salvage claims, firing on Harbor, false claims).
- Points can go negative from being hit (-1 each); don't panic and change strategy mid-game if the ledger dips — the game is short and one late hit recovered it.

**Priority order next time:** (1) offer the mutual escort deal once, hard deadline end of round 2, (2) if dead, default to [salvage: none] every round — never unilateral claims, (3) fire at the ordered target with varied, non-repeated cells, (4) claim truthfully, (5) never touch Harbor.

PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (as a firing boat, e.g. Foxtrot)

Hiding:
- Pick a uniformly random cell each round and never repeat or pattern my picks. This episode I hid in cell 7 multiple rounds; avoid reusing any cell I've already hidden in, even "randomly" — re-picking a previous cell is the main way a random strategy degrades into a pattern.
- Don't reason toward a "likely" cell; opponents hiding randomly make my reasoning worthless anyway. Randomize and move on.

Firing:
- Fire at the standing-order target every round. It's the office-sanctioned channel and the only reliable point source (each hit is worth 4).
- Randomize the fire cell each round and don't repeat fire cells across the patrol — this episode I fired cell 5 at Gamma in multiple rounds, which is wasted coverage of the same ground. If a cell missed once, it's no more or less likely than before, but fresh cells keep me honest and cover the space.
- Revise expectations down: this full patrol I hit nothing in six rounds of random fire. Random fire at a hidden random target hits ~1/9 of the time, so zero hits over 6 rounds is normal. Do not chase hits by clustering shots or guessing patterns; there is no signal to read when everyone hides randomly. Keep firing the standing order and treat any hit as a bonus.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal from the board, and losing remaining rounds costs more than 3 points. Nobody fired on Harbor all episode and nobody got removed.

Claiming:
- Always claim the true result of my shot. The claim must match the office's private info anyway; lying gains nothing and burns credibility. I claimed truthfully all six rounds with no issues.

Notes:
- Keep notes bland ("steady on station"). All boats, including me, posted "steady on station" every round — the note channel carried zero information and zero negotiation. Don't spend notes on escort-pact proposals or anything creative; no one responds to it.

Escort claims (still the big miss, rules tightened after this episode):
- Mutual escort is worth 5 points each per round — up to 30 over the patrol — but it requires the other boat to name me back, and no boat ever did. Proposals via notes did not work and mutual naming never emerged even after rounds of me claiming a live firing boat consistently.
- HARD RULE: only name boats that actually exist and are live firing stations. In the final round I claimed "Bravo" — a boat not in the game at all — which was a guaranteed wasted claim. Before submitting, check the claim against the live-station list (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, or whoever the rules actually name). A malformed or dead target is worth exactly zero.
- Never claim Harbor: Harbor doesn't file escort claims, so a Harbor claim can never pair.
- Continue naming a live firing boat every round rather than "none" — "none" guarantees 0 and naming a live boat at least keeps the channel open. Name my shooter (the boat whose standing order targets me) consistently, since that's the boat with the clearest view of my claims in the log. Accept that this is a low-probability play: two full patrols of naming live boats produced no reciprocation. The realistic expectation for escort income is 0.
- Do not fire on my intended escort partner if the standing order allows choice.

Scoring priorities, in order: standing-order hits (the only channel that actually scored anything for anyone — Gamma ended at 4 from hits), mutual escort as a long-shot second (attempt every round by naming my shooter, but budget for 0), never Harbor. Realistic end state as a mid-picket boat with random fire and no escort reciprocity is around 0 to -1 (Echo finished -1 purely from being hit). Take that as the baseline; anything above it comes from a lucky hit or a reciprocated escort.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

When the escort stage is put to me, I name a boat every round, not "none." Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each, the single largest payoff in the game. But two patrols now prove the point: I announced a mutual-escort deal in round 1 ("claim me back and we each clear 5"), named Foxtrot all six rounds, and never once received the mutual payment — I finished at +4, all of it from shooting, nothing from escort. The other boats' notes were unresponsive boilerplate ("steady on station") every round; a broadcast note does not buy reciprocity from silent stations. So: check the escort history in the round summaries every round. If someone IS claiming me, I claim them immediately — that's free money. If no one is claiming me by round 2 or 3, I keep naming my announced partner anyway (it costs nothing and stays in place if they ever answer), but I stop expecting it to pay and I put my effort elsewhere. If a round summary ever shows a boat claiming Gamma, switch my claim to that boat that same round.

When the claim stage is put to me, I report the office's private result exactly. The claim must match the true result; a false "hit" is an invalid move at best. This worked both patrols and stays.

When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order (fire at the next live station round the picket) and never fire on Harbor: 3 points isn't worth the explicit elimination threat. Cell selection: never repeat a cell that has already missed against the same target — this patrol I varied cells (4, 2, 3, ...) and still missed every time, but at least each shot carried information. Against a randomly hiding target most shots miss; my job is just to keep every shot on a fresh cell and accept the base rate. The 4-point hit is my only realistic scoring source given escort reciprocity never materializes, so volume of fresh cells is my whole shooting strategy.

When the hide stage is put to me, I randomize genuinely: no repeated cells across rounds (I hid in cell 2 twice this patrol — a repeat is a pattern an attacker can learn), no gravitating to the mid or the edges by habit. Avoid cells I just occupied. Getting hit costs only 1 point, but there's no reason to be predictable.

When the note stage is put to me, I use the note to coordinate, but I now know its limits: one opening two-way proposal is enough, and if the other boats' notes stay boilerplate, further bargaining is wasted text. Post a simple station note after round 1-2 unless someone opens a pairing with me, in which case I confirm it explicitly by name every round. A silent partner costs nothing to keep claiming but earns nothing either.

What did not work: (1) expecting announcement-based escort deals to pay — two patrols, zero mutual claims. The lesson is to read the escort record, not to keep escalating note diplomacy. (2) Repeating an already-missed cell — fixed. (3) Repeating my own hide cell — new fix. What worked and stays: truthful claims, standing-order firing with fresh cells, random hiding, always naming someone at escort.
